SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Paper burning to ash

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — 100 °C

2. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

3. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

6. B — Glucose and oxygen

7. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

10. B — Ice melting to water

11. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

12. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Slopes as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Change of State; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Composition of Air; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
